title: Training Note: The Wage Basis of an Estimated Assessment
content:
**Rule.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, the wage basis of an estimated assessment follows the pattern of the employer's reports:

- when the taxable wages on the most recently filed original report are at least 1.2 times the average taxable wages of the original reports filed within the recent report months, 12, the basis is that most recent report's taxable wages;
- when that test is not met and fewer original reports than a year's quarters, 4, were filed within the recent 12 months, the basis is the average taxable wages of the original reports filed within the longer report months, 24;
- otherwise the basis is the average taxable wages of the original reports filed within the recent 12 months.

The windows are counted in whole months back from the day the estimate is booked, by the filing dates of the reports, and an average taken over a window in which no original report was filed is zero. "Most recently filed" means the original report with the latest filing date. Amended reports play no part.

## Decision table

| Latest original report's taxable wages at least 1.2 times the 12-month average | Original reports filed within 12 months | Wage basis |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Any number | The latest original report's taxable wages |
| No | Fewer than 4 | Average of the original reports filed within 24 months |
| No | 4 or more | Average of the original reports filed within 12 months |

## Questions and answers (hypothetical figures)

**The 12-month average is USD 50,000.00 and the latest original report shows USD 60,000.00. What is the basis?** 60,000.00 is exactly 1.2 times 50,000.00, which is "at least", so the basis is USD 60,000.00.

**Same average, latest report USD 59,999.99, and only 3 original reports filed within 12 months?** The first test is not met, and 3 is fewer than 4, so the basis is the average of the original reports filed within 24 months. If those were 5 reports with taxable wages adding to USD 240,000.00, the basis is USD 48,000.00.

**Same average and latest report, but 4 original reports filed within 12 months?** The first test is not met and the count is not fewer than 4, so the basis is the 12-month average, USD 50,000.00.

**No original report was filed within 12 months at all?** The 12-month average is then zero, and any most recent report's taxable wages are at least 1.2 times zero; the basis is the taxable wages of the most recently filed original report.
